images.caption: Commonwealth Railways G class locomotive no. G18 with the Trans-Australian Express, at Cook, South Australia, on the Trans-Australian Railway.The locomotive was built by Toowoomba Foundry, Toowoomba, Queensland, Australia. images.filename: Commonwealth Railways G class locomotive and Trans-Australian Express at Tarcoola, circa 1925.jpg
images.caption: A Commonwealth Railways G class locomotive with a westbound Trans-Australian Express, at Tarcoola, South Australia, on the Trans-Australian Railway.The number of the locomotive is not clear, but it appears to be G20, which was built by Toowoomba Foundry, Toowoomba, Queensland, Australia.  G20 entered service in June 1917, and was officially withdrawn in May 1952.  At the time this photo was taken early in its service life, it had a kerosene headlight.Some of the information provided here about the image is obtained from Fluck, Ronald E; Marshall, Barry; Wilson, John (1996). Locomotives and Railcars of the Commonwealth Railways. Welland, SA: Gresley Publishing, pp. 25-29. ISBN 0959969039.
images.alt: A Commonwealth Railways G class locomotive with a westbound Trans-Australian Express, at Tarcoola, South Australia, on the Trans-Australian Railway.The number of the locomotive is not clear, but it appears to be G20, which was built by Toowoomba Foundry, Toowoomba, Queensland, Australia.  G20 entered service in June 1917, and was officially withdrawn in May 1952.  At the time this photo was taken early in its service life, it had a kerosene headlight.Some of the information provided here about the image is obtained from Fluck, Ronald E; Marshall, Barry; Wilson, John (1996). images.caption:
1 Station Street, Mount Victoria.
Taken from car window. 
Opened in October 1878 as a Resort Hotel, the Imperial is the oldest Tourist Hotel in Australia.

By the early 1900s,it was well established as one of the three Grand Hotels of the Blue Mountains, along with the Carrington at Katoomba and the Hydro at Medlow Bath.   In its heyday, The Imperial hosted Prime Ministers and Royalty, and still proudly displays the Royal Coat of Arms presented in 1901.
